title: Certify a plan from complementary slackness

blocks.text: A print shop's scheduler is handed weekly plans by three sales offices, each sure its plan is the most profitable. The shop has no solver licence on the scheduling machine, but it has NumPy. It wants a function that either proves a plan optimal, by producing prices that certify it, or refuses it.

The shop's LP, with $`A`$ the products, $`R`$ the rows (each a limit $`\le`$ or a minimum $`\ge`$), $`v_j`$ the profit per run of product $`j`$, $`a_{ij}`$ its coefficient in row $`i`$ (0 if absent) and $`b_i`$ the right-hand side:
\max \sum_{j \in A} v_j\, x_j \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j \in A} a_{ij}\, x_j \;(\le \text{ or } \ge)\; b_i \;\; \forall i \in R, \qquad x_j \ge 0
For a feasible plan $`x`$, complementary slackness fixes the prices it implies:

items: $`y_i = 0`$ for every row with slack ($`|\sum_j a_{ij} x_j - b_i| > `$ `tol`);
for every product with $`x_j > `$ `tol`, its reduced cost is zero: $`\sum_{i \text{ binding}} a_{ij}\, y_i = v_j`$, one linear equation per used product in the prices of the binding rows.

blocks.text: The plan is optimal exactly when those prices are dual feasible: $`y_i \ge 0`$ on every $`\le`$ row, $`y_i \le 0`$ on every $`\ge`$ row, and every product's reduced cost $`v_j - \sum_{i \in R} a_{ij}\, y_i \le 0`$ (all three with tolerance `tol`).

Write `certify(value, rows, plan, tol=1e-6)` in `certify.py`. `value` maps each product to $`v_j`$; `rows` maps each row's name to `(coefficients, sense, rhs)`; `plan` maps each product to $`x_j`$. Return a dict of every row's price when the plan is optimal, and `None` when it is not. Every plan the tests pass is feasible and has as many binding rows as used products, with a system that has one solution, so `np.linalg.solve(matrix, rhs)` solves it.

cases.says: the optimal plan gets the prices that prove it, and a feasible plan whose implied prices have a wrong sign gets None
a binding >= row's price must be at most zero, and a negative one is no reason to refuse
prices with the right signs still refuse the plan when a product it leaves out has a positive reduced cost

origin.section: Complementary Slackness Certifies a Plan Without a Solver

concepts: prices derived from a plan by complementary slackness prove it optimal when they are dual feasible
